**[GROUND LEASE AGREEMENT]{.underline}**

**[Antelope Ridge Solar Project]{.underline}**

**Between**

**DUNLAP FARMING COMPANY LLC** a California limited liability company (\"Landlord\")

**and**

**RIDGECREST ENERGY PARTNERS LLC** a Delaware limited liability company qualified to do business in California (\"Tenant\")

**Dated: March 8, 2022**

**Property: Approximately 1,480 Acres, Lancaster, Los Angeles County, California**

Recorded with the Los Angeles County Recorder\'s Office Document No. 2022-0341876

**GROUND LEASE AGREEMENT**

This Ground Lease Agreement (this \"Lease\") is entered into as of March 8, 2022 (the \"Effective Date\"), by and between **Dunlap Farming Company LLC**, a California limited liability company (\"Landlord\"), and **Ridgecrest Energy Partners LLC**, a Delaware limited liability company qualified to do business in the State of California (\"Tenant\"). Landlord and Tenant are sometimes referred to herein individually as a \"Party\" and collectively as the \"Parties.\"

**[RECITALS]{.underline}**

**WHEREAS**, Landlord is the fee simple owner of certain real property located in Lancaster, Los Angeles County, California, more particularly described in Exhibit A attached hereto and incorporated herein by this reference (the \"Premises\"), consisting of approximately one thousand four hundred eighty (1,480) acres, identified by Los Angeles County Assessor\'s Parcel Numbers APN 3201-014-007 (approximately 640 acres), APN 3201-014-008 (approximately 520 acres), and APN 3201-014-011 (approximately 320 acres);

**WHEREAS**, Tenant is a utility-scale solar energy developer headquartered at 2750 Jamboree Road, Suite 1400, Irvine, California 92660, with a portfolio of operating and under-development solar photovoltaic projects across the states of California, Nevada, and Arizona, and Tenant possesses the technical expertise, financial resources, and industry experience necessary to develop, construct, and operate large-scale solar energy generation facilities;

**WHEREAS**, Tenant desires to lease the Premises from Landlord for the purpose of developing, constructing, owning, operating, maintaining, and ultimately decommissioning a solar photovoltaic electricity generating facility with a nameplate capacity of approximately two hundred megawatts direct current (200 MW DC) (the \"Project\"), together with all associated improvements, equipment, battery energy storage systems, electrical interconnection facilities, substations, access roads, meteorological equipment, and ancillary structures necessary or useful in connection therewith;

**WHEREAS**, Landlord desires to lease the Premises to Tenant upon the terms and conditions set forth herein, and the Parties have negotiated this Lease at arm\'s length and in good faith;

**WHEREAS**, Tenant anticipates financing the development and construction of the Project through one or more project finance lenders, tax equity investors, and other institutional capital sources, and the Parties acknowledge and agree that the terms and conditions of this Lease are intended to be acceptable to, and in a form customarily required by, such project finance lenders and tax equity investors as a condition to providing financing for the Project (collectively, the standard of \"Bankability\"); and

**WHEREAS**, the Premises are currently zoned A-2 (Heavy Agriculture) under the Los Angeles County Zoning Ordinance, and Tenant has obtained from the Los Angeles County Department of Regional Planning a conditional use permit, designated as CUP No. 2021-1294, authorizing the development, construction, and operation of a solar energy generation facility on the Premises, which CUP was approved on November 18, 2021 and has become final and non-appealable.

**NOW, THEREFORE**, in consideration of the mutual covenants, promises, and agreements contained herein, and for other good and valuable consideration, the receipt and sufficiency of which are hereby acknowledged, the Parties agree as follows:

**[ARTICLE 1 --- DEFINITIONS]{.underline}**

The following terms shall have the meanings set forth below when used in this Lease. Capitalized terms used but not defined in this Article 1 shall have the meanings ascribed to them elsewhere in this Lease.

**\"Affiliate\"** means, with respect to any Person, any other Person that directly or indirectly controls, is controlled by, or is under common control with, such Person. For purposes of this definition, \"control\" means the ownership of fifty percent (50%) or more of the outstanding voting interests of such Person or the power, whether by contract, equity ownership, or otherwise, to direct or cause the direction of the management and policies of such Person.

**\"Base Rent\"** has the meaning set forth in Section 4.2.

**\"BESS\"** means a battery energy storage system.

**\"CAISO\"** means the California Independent System Operator Corporation.

**\"COD\"** or **\"Commercial Operation Date\"** means the date on which the Project has been (a) mechanically complete in all material respects, (b) interconnected to the electric grid in accordance with the applicable interconnection agreement, and (c) has generated electricity for delivery under its power purchase agreement for a continuous period of not less than five (5) consecutive days.

**\"Commencement Date\"** has the meaning set forth in Section 3.2.

**\"CUP\"** means Conditional Use Permit No. 2021-1294 issued by the Los Angeles County Department of Regional Planning, as may be amended from time to time.

**\"Decommissioning\"** has the meaning set forth in Article 14.

**\"Decommissioning Period\"** has the meaning set forth in Section 14.1.

**\"Effective Date\"** means March 8, 2022.

**\"Event of Default\"** has the meaning set forth in Section 12.1.

**\"Extension Term\"** has the meaning set forth in Section 3.3.

**\"Force Majeure\"** means any event or circumstance beyond a Party\'s reasonable control that prevents or delays such Party\'s performance of its obligations under this Lease, including, without limitation, acts of God, fire, flood, earthquake, drought, storm, hurricane, tornado, volcanic eruption, epidemic, pandemic, war (whether declared or undeclared), armed conflict, terrorism, sabotage, riot, civil disturbance, insurrection, strikes, lockouts, labor disputes, governmental actions or orders (including moratoria, embargoes, and sanctions), changes in applicable law, interconnection delays beyond Tenant\'s reasonable control, CAISO queue delays, curtailment orders by any governmental authority or grid operator, casualty, condemnation, and any other events of a similar nature beyond the reasonable control of the affected Party. Force Majeure shall not include financial inability to perform or changes in market conditions.

**\"Improvement Area\"** means that portion of the Premises shown on Exhibit B on which Tenant is permitted to install Project improvements.

**\"Initial Term\"** has the meaning set forth in Section 3.1.

**\"Leasehold Mortgage\"** has the meaning set forth in Section 10.1.

**\"Leasehold Mortgagee\"** has the meaning set forth in Section 10.1.

**\"Option Period\"** has the meaning set forth in Section 3.5.

**\"Permitted Exceptions\"** means the exceptions to title set forth in Exhibit D.

**\"Permitted Transfer\"** has the meaning set forth in Section 9.2.

**\"Person\"** means any natural person, corporation, limited liability company, partnership, joint venture, trust, governmental entity, or other entity.

**\"Premises\"** means the real property described in Exhibit A.

**\"Project\"** means the solar photovoltaic electricity generating facility and all related improvements, equipment, BESS components, interconnection facilities, substations, access roads, meteorological equipment, fencing, and ancillary structures to be developed, constructed, owned, operated, maintained, and decommissioned by Tenant on the Premises.

**\"Rent\"** means, collectively, the Option Period Rent, Base Rent, and any other amounts payable by Tenant to Landlord under this Lease.

**\"Restoration\"** has the meaning set forth in Section 14.2.

**\"Security Deposit\"** has the meaning set forth in Section 5.1.

**\"SNDA\"** has the meaning set forth in Section 10.3.

**\"Tenant Improvements\"** means all structures, equipment, solar panels, racking and tracker systems, inverters, transformers, substations, BESS components, fencing, access roads, foundations, piles, cable and conduit, meteorological towers, communication equipment, and all other improvements of any kind installed by or on behalf of Tenant on the Premises in connection with the Project.

**\"Term\"** means, collectively, the Initial Term and any Extension Terms.

**[ARTICLE 2 --- LEASE OF PREMISES]{.underline}**

**Section 2.1 --- Grant of Lease**

Landlord hereby leases to Tenant, and Tenant hereby leases from Landlord, the Premises for the purpose of developing, constructing, owning, operating, maintaining, repairing, replacing, repowering, and ultimately decommissioning the Project, upon and subject to the terms and conditions set forth in this Lease. The lease granted hereunder includes all rights reasonably necessary for the intended use of the Premises, including, without limitation, (a) the right of ingress and egress over the Premises and over Landlord\'s adjacent parcels as shown on the access easement map attached as Exhibit C (the \"Access Easement\"), (b) the right to receive and utilize solar irradiance on and above the Premises, (c) the right to install, maintain, and operate electrical transmission and interconnection lines across the Premises to the point of interconnection with the electric grid, and (d) the right to use, control, and manage the surface and airspace of the Premises in connection with the Project.

**Section 2.2 --- Permitted Uses**

Tenant may use the Premises for the following purposes, and for all uses ancillary, incidental, or related thereto: (a) solar photovoltaic energy generation; (b) battery energy storage; (c) electrical transmission, interconnection, and distribution of electricity; (d) meteorological testing and monitoring; (e) environmental monitoring, assessment, and remediation; (f) construction staging, laydown, and materials storage; (g) installation and maintenance of fencing, security systems, and surveillance equipment; (h) installation and maintenance of access roads and parking areas; and (i) all other activities reasonably necessary for the development, construction, operation, maintenance, repair, repowering, replacement, and decommissioning of the Project.

**Section 2.3 --- Quiet Enjoyment**

Landlord covenants and warrants that, so long as Tenant is not in default under this Lease beyond applicable notice and cure periods, Tenant shall have quiet and peaceful possession of the Premises throughout the Term, free from interference, disturbance, or molestation by Landlord or any Person claiming by, through, or under Landlord. Landlord shall defend Tenant\'s right to quiet enjoyment against all Persons claiming an interest in the Premises by, through, or under Landlord.

**Section 2.4 --- Landlord\'s Retained Rights**

Landlord retains fee title to the Premises and all mineral, oil, gas, and subsurface rights beneath the surface of the Premises. Notwithstanding the foregoing, Landlord hereby covenants and agrees that neither Landlord nor any third party claiming by, through, or under Landlord shall conduct, permit, or authorize any surface operations, drilling, extraction, mining, blasting, exploration, or other activities on or affecting the surface of the Premises, or that would interfere with or impair Tenant\'s use and enjoyment of the Premises or the operation of the Project, at any time during the Term (the \"No Surface Use Covenant\"). The No Surface Use Covenant shall be binding upon Landlord, its successors, assigns, and all Persons claiming by, through, or under Landlord, and shall be deemed a covenant running with the land for the duration of the Term. In the event of any conflict between Landlord\'s retained mineral rights and Tenant\'s rights under this Lease, the provisions of this Lease (including the No Surface Use Covenant) shall control. Additionally, Landlord shall not conduct or permit any agricultural operations, grazing, crop production, or other farming activities on the Premises during the Term.

**Section 2.5 --- Landlord Access**

Landlord and its authorized agents, consultants, and representatives may access the Premises for the purpose of inspecting the condition of the Premises, verifying Tenant\'s compliance with this Lease, and conducting environmental assessments, upon not less than forty-eight (48) hours\' prior written notice to Tenant (which notice may be delivered by email to Tenant\'s designated operations contact), during normal business hours (8:00 a.m. to 5:00 p.m., Monday through Friday, excluding legal holidays), and subject to Tenant\'s reasonable safety and security protocols. Landlord\'s personnel and invitees accessing the Premises shall at all times comply with all applicable safety regulations, including Occupational Safety and Health Administration (\"OSHA\") requirements and Tenant\'s site-specific safety plan, and shall be accompanied by a Tenant representative at all times while within the Improvement Area or any active construction zone. Landlord shall not interfere with the ongoing operations of the Project during any inspection. In the event of an emergency threatening imminent harm to persons or property, Landlord may access the Premises without prior notice, provided that Landlord shall (a) use commercially reasonable efforts to notify Tenant by telephone or email as soon as practicable and (b) provide Tenant with written notice describing the nature of the emergency and the scope of access within twenty-four (24) hours thereafter. Landlord\'s access rights under this Section shall not be exercised so as to unreasonably interfere with or disrupt the construction, operation, or maintenance of the Project.

**[ARTICLE 3 --- TERM]{.underline}**

**Section 3.1 --- Initial Term**

The initial term of this Lease shall commence on the Commencement Date and shall continue for a period of thirty (30) years, expiring on the thirtieth (30th) anniversary of the Commencement Date, unless sooner terminated or extended as provided herein (the \"Initial Term\").

**Section 3.2 --- Commencement Date**

The \"Commencement Date\" shall be the earlier of: (a) the Commercial Operation Date, or (b) the date that is thirty-six (36) months after the Effective Date. If Tenant has not achieved COD by the date that is thirty-six (36) months after the Effective Date, the Commencement Date shall be deemed to have occurred on such date, and Base Rent shall begin to accrue as of such date regardless of whether COD has been achieved; provided, however, that if the delay in achieving COD is directly attributable to Force Majeure (including, without limitation, delays in the CAISO interconnection queue, delays in governmental permit issuance not caused by Tenant\'s failure to submit timely or complete applications, or delays caused by pandemic-related supply chain disruptions), then the thirty-six (36) month period shall be extended on a day-for-day basis by the duration of such Force Majeure event, up to a maximum extension of twelve (12) additional months (for a total maximum period of forty-eight (48) months from the Effective Date). Tenant shall provide Landlord with written notice of any Force Majeure event claimed to extend the Commencement Date within thirty (30) days of Tenant\'s becoming aware of such event, together with reasonable supporting documentation.

**Section 3.3 --- Extension Terms**

Tenant shall have the right, exercisable at Tenant\'s sole option, to extend the term of this Lease for two (2) additional consecutive periods of five (5) years each (each, an \"Extension Term\"), by delivering irrevocable written notice to Landlord no less than twelve (12) months and no more than twenty-four (24) months prior to the scheduled expiration of the then-current term. Each Extension Term shall be on the same terms and conditions as set forth in this Lease, except that Base Rent during each Extension Term shall be determined in accordance with Section 4.4. The extension options granted under this Section are personal to Tenant and its Permitted Transferees and any Leasehold Mortgagee or its designee, and may not be severed from this Lease. The exercise of the first Extension Term shall not obligate Tenant to exercise the second Extension Term.

**Section 3.4 --- Total Potential Term**

The total potential term of this Lease, including both Extension Terms if exercised, is forty (40) years (consisting of a thirty (30) year Initial Term plus two (2) Extension Terms of five (5) years each), plus any Decommissioning Period following expiration of the Term.

**Section 3.5 --- Option Period**

The period from the Effective Date through the Commencement Date shall constitute the \"Option Period,\" during which Tenant shall have the right to conduct all due diligence, environmental studies, Phase I and Phase II environmental site assessments, geotechnical testing, cultural resources surveys, biological assessments, topographic surveys, meteorological monitoring, permitting activities, interconnection studies, and pre-construction work on the Premises as Tenant deems necessary or appropriate. Tenant\'s right to access and use the Premises during the Option Period shall be subject to Tenant\'s payment of Option Period Rent as set forth in Section 4.1.

**Section 3.6 --- Construction Commencement Deadline**

Tenant shall commence physical construction of the Project (defined as the mobilization of heavy construction equipment onto the Premises and commencement of grading, civil earthwork, or pile driving activities) no later than twenty-four (24) months after the Effective Date. If Tenant fails to commence physical construction by such date, Landlord may terminate this Lease upon ninety (90) days\' prior written notice to Tenant, provided that (a) if such delay is caused by Force Majeure, the deadline shall be extended on a day-for-day basis by the duration of such Force Majeure event, and (b) Tenant shall have the right to cure such failure during the ninety (90) day notice period by commencing physical construction prior to the expiration of such period, in which case Landlord\'s termination notice shall be deemed withdrawn and of no further force or effect.

**[ARTICLE 4 --- RENT]{.underline}**

**Section 4.1 --- Option Period Rent**

During the Option Period, Tenant shall pay Landlord annual rent of Fifty Dollars (\$50.00) per acre per year (\"Option Period Rent\"), payable in advance in equal monthly installments on or before the first business day of each calendar month. Based on the approximately 1,480 acres comprising the Premises, the annual Option Period Rent is Seventy-Four Thousand Dollars (\$74,000), and the monthly installment is Six Thousand One Hundred Sixty-Seven Dollars (\$6,167) (rounded to the nearest dollar). Option Period Rent shall be prorated for any partial month at the beginning or end of the Option Period. The Option Period shall not exceed thirty-six (36) months from the Effective Date (or forty-eight (48) months in the event of a Force Majeure extension under Section 3.2).

**Section 4.2 --- Base Rent**

Commencing on the Commencement Date and continuing throughout the Initial Term and any Extension Terms, Tenant shall pay Landlord annual base rent of Nine Hundred Dollars (\$900.00) per acre per year (the \"Base Rent\"). Based on the approximately 1,480 acres comprising the Premises, the initial annual Base Rent is One Million Three Hundred Thirty-Two Thousand Dollars (\$1,332,000). Base Rent shall be payable in advance in equal monthly installments of One Hundred Eleven Thousand Dollars (\$111,000) on the first business day of each calendar month. Base Rent for any partial month at the beginning or end of the Term shall be prorated on a per diem basis.

**Section 4.3 --- Escalation**

Base Rent shall increase by two percent (2.0%) per annum on each anniversary of the Commencement Date, calculated on a simple (non-compounding) basis applied to the initial annual Base Rent amount. For clarity, the Base Rent for Year N of the Term (where Year 1 is the period commencing on the Commencement Date) shall be calculated as follows:

> Year \[N\] Base Rent = Initial Base Rent × (1 + 0.02 × (N -- 1))

By way of illustration:

  -----------------------------------------------------------------------
  **Year**                **Calculation**         **Annual Base Rent**
  ----------------------- ----------------------- -----------------------
  1                       \$1,332,000 × 1.00      \$1,332,000

  5                       \$1,332,000 × 1.08      \$1,438,560

  10                      \$1,332,000 × 1.18      \$1,571,760

  15                      \$1,332,000 × 1.28      \$1,704,960

  20                      \$1,332,000 × 1.38      \$1,838,160

  25                      \$1,332,000 × 1.48      \$1,971,360

  30                      \$1,332,000 × 1.58      \$2,104,560
  -----------------------------------------------------------------------

The simple escalation methodology set forth in this Section ensures that annual rent increases are predictable and proportionate over the Initial Term.

**Section 4.4 --- Extension Term Rent**

During each Extension Term, the Base Rent shall be the greater of: (a) the Base Rent payable in the final year of the immediately preceding term (including all escalations accrued therein), or (b) the Fair Market Rental Value of the Premises for solar energy use, as determined in accordance with this Section. The Fair Market Rental Value shall be determined by an independent MAI-certified appraiser mutually agreed upon by Landlord and Tenant. If the Parties cannot agree upon a single appraiser within thirty (30) days after Tenant\'s exercise of the applicable Extension Term option, then each Party shall, within fifteen (15) days thereafter, select one MAI-certified appraiser, and the two appraisers so selected shall, within fifteen (15) days after their appointment, select a third MAI-certified appraiser. Each appraiser shall independently determine the Fair Market Rental Value. The Fair Market Rental Value shall be the average of the two closest appraisals. The Parties shall share equally in the cost of the appraisal process. The escalation methodology set forth in Section 4.3 shall apply during each Extension Term, calculated from the Extension Term Base Rent as determined hereunder.

**Section 4.5 --- Revenue Sharing**

\[Intentionally Omitted.\] There shall be no revenue share, percentage rent, production-based payment, or any similar payment in addition to the Base Rent and other Rent expressly provided for in this Lease. The Parties have negotiated the Base Rent and escalation methodology set forth herein as the sole and complete compensation to Landlord for the use and occupancy of the Premises.

**Section 4.6 --- Rent Abatement**

If Tenant is unable to operate the Project for a continuous period of ninety (90) days or more due to an event of Force Majeure, Base Rent shall be abated on a pro rata basis for the period beginning on the ninety-first (91st) day following the commencement of such Force Majeure event and continuing until the earlier of (a) the date the Force Majeure event ceases or (b) the date Tenant resumes commercial operation of the Project. Any Rent abated pursuant to this Section shall not be subject to recoupment, recapture, or clawback by Landlord. Tenant shall provide Landlord with prompt written notice of any Force Majeure event for which Tenant intends to claim a rent abatement, together with reasonable supporting documentation.

**Section 4.7 --- Late Payment**

Any Rent payment or other monetary obligation due under this Lease that is not received by Landlord within ten (10) business days after the date such payment is due shall bear interest at the rate of one and one-half percent (1.5%) per month (or, if less, the maximum rate permitted by applicable law) from the original due date until such payment is received by Landlord. The assessment of late payment interest under this Section shall not constitute a waiver of any default or limit Landlord\'s other remedies under this Lease.

**[ARTICLE 5 --- SECURITY DEPOSIT]{.underline}**

**Section 5.1 --- Amount and Form**

Within thirty (30) days after the Effective Date, Tenant shall deliver to Landlord a security deposit in the form of an irrevocable standby letter of credit issued by a commercial bank with a long-term credit rating of not less than \"A-\" (or equivalent) from Standard & Poor\'s, Moody\'s, or Fitch Ratings, in the amount of Seven Hundred Ninety-Eight Thousand Dollars (\$798,000), representing approximately six (6) months of initial annual Base Rent (the \"Security Deposit\"). The letter of credit shall be in form and substance reasonably acceptable to Landlord, shall name Landlord as beneficiary, shall have an initial term of not less than one (1) year, and shall include an automatic annual renewal provision with a sixty (60) day \"evergreen\" clause providing that the issuing bank shall give Landlord not less than sixty (60) days\' prior written notice of any non-renewal or cancellation.

**Section 5.2 --- Draws**

Landlord may draw upon the Security Deposit only upon the occurrence of an uncured Event of Default by Tenant and only to the extent of actual damages sustained by Landlord as a direct result of such Event of Default. Prior to making any draw on the Security Deposit, Landlord shall provide Tenant with at least ten (10) business days\' prior written notice specifying (a) the nature of the Event of Default, (b) the amount Landlord intends to draw, and (c) a reasonable description of the actual damages for which the draw is being made. Landlord shall not make any draw if Tenant cures the underlying Event of Default within the ten (10) business day notice period.

**Section 5.3 --- Replenishment**

If Landlord draws upon the Security Deposit in accordance with Section 5.2, Tenant shall replenish the Security Deposit to its full required amount within thirty (30) days after receipt of written notice from Landlord of such draw, together with documentation of the actual amounts drawn and the application of such funds.

**Section 5.4 --- Reduction After COD**

Upon the second (2nd) anniversary of COD, provided that no uncured Event of Default then exists, the required amount of the Security Deposit shall be reduced to an amount equal to three (3) months of the then-current annual Base Rent. Tenant may replace the existing letter of credit with a letter of credit in the reduced amount that otherwise complies with the requirements of Section 5.1.

**Section 5.5 --- Return**

Within sixty (60) days following the later of (a) the expiration or earlier termination of this Lease and (b) Tenant\'s completion of all Decommissioning and Restoration obligations under Article 14, Landlord shall return or release the Security Deposit (or any remaining balance thereof, net of any amounts drawn in accordance with this Article 5 and not yet replenished) to Tenant, together with a written statement of any amounts retained and the basis therefor.

**[ARTICLE 6 --- TAXES AND ASSESSMENTS]{.underline}**

**Section 6.1 --- Real Property Taxes**

Tenant shall be responsible for and shall timely pay all real property taxes, assessments, special assessments, and governmental charges of any kind levied or assessed against the Premises or the Tenant Improvements during the Term that are attributable to the Tenant Improvements or the solar energy use of the Premises. Landlord shall remain responsible for real property taxes attributable to the underlying land value of the Premises as if unimproved and not subject to this Lease. If real property taxes are not separately assessed with respect to the Tenant Improvements and the underlying land, the Parties shall cooperate in good faith to allocate such taxes in a manner consistent with this Section based on the assessed value attributable to each component.

**Section 6.2 --- Personal Property Taxes**

Tenant shall pay all personal property taxes levied or assessed against Tenant\'s equipment, machinery, fixtures, and other personal property located on the Premises.

**Section 6.3 --- Tax Contest**

Tenant shall have the right, at Tenant\'s sole cost and expense, to contest in good faith and by appropriate legal proceedings the validity, applicability, or amount of any tax, assessment, or charge for which Tenant is responsible under this Article, provided that (a) such contest shall not subject Landlord or the Premises to any risk of forfeiture, penalty, or lien, and (b) Tenant shall post adequate security or bond for the contested amount during the pendency of such contest.

**[ARTICLE 7 --- INSURANCE]{.underline}**

**Section 7.1 --- Tenant\'s Insurance**

Tenant shall obtain and maintain throughout the Term, at Tenant\'s sole cost and expense, the following insurance coverages:

> \(a\) **Commercial General Liability Insurance** with limits of not less than Ten Million Dollars (\$10,000,000) per occurrence and Twenty Million Dollars (\$20,000,000) in the annual aggregate, covering bodily injury, property damage, personal injury, and advertising injury arising from Tenant\'s operations on the Premises.
>
> \(b\) **Property/Builder\'s Risk Insurance** covering all Tenant Improvements for their full replacement cost on an all-risk basis, including coverage for flood, earthquake, windstorm, and equipment breakdown.
>
> \(c\) **Pollution Liability Insurance** with limits of not less than Ten Million Dollars (\$10,000,000) per occurrence and

139	> \(b\) **Non-Monetary Default.** Tenant\'s failure to perform or observe any non-monetary obligation, covenant, or condition under this Lease within sixty (60) days after Tenant\'s receipt of written notice from Landlord specifying such failure in reasonable detail; provided, however, that if the nature of such failure is such that it cannot reasonably be cured within such sixty (60) day period, it shall not constitute an Event of Default if Tenant commences the cure within such sixty (60) day period and thereafter diligently and continuously prosecutes the cure to completion within a reasonable time (not to exceed an additional one hundred twenty (120) days, except in the case of Decommissioning obligations, which shall be subject to the timelines in Article 14).

142	>
143	> \(d\) **Abandonment.** Tenant shall abandon the Premises (as determined by the cessation of all Project operations and maintenance activities) for a continuous period of twelve (12) months or more, excluding any period during which operations are suspended due to Force Majeure, scheduled maintenance, repowering, or technology replacement.

153	> \(c\) Exercise any other rights and remedies available to Landlord under applicable California law.

155	The rights and remedies of Landlord set forth herein are cumulative and not exclusive of any other rights or remedies available at law or in equity.

158	
159	If Landlord fails to perform any material obligation under this Lease, Tenant shall give Landlord written notice specifying the nature of such failure in reasonable detail. If Landlord does not cure such failure within thirty (30) days after receipt of such notice (or, if such failure is of a nature that cannot reasonably be cured within thirty (30) days, within such longer period as is reasonably necessary, provided Landlord commences the cure within such thirty (30) day period and diligently prosecutes the cure to completion), then Tenant may, at its option: (a) cure such failure on Landlord\'s behalf and offset the reasonable, documented costs of such cure against Rent next coming due (with interest at the rate set forth in Section 4.7); (b) terminate this Lease upon sixty (60) days\' written notice to Landlord; or (c) pursue damages at law or in equity.

162

Tenant\'s sole obligation upon any termination shall be to (a) complete Decommissioning and Restoration in accordance with Article 14, (b) pay all Rent and other monetary obligations accrued and unpaid through the effective date of termination, and (c) pay damages, if any, to which Landlord is entitled under applicable law. This Section shall survive termination.

166	
167	No waiver by either Party of any default or breach of any term, covenant, or condition of this Lease shall be deemed a waiver of any subsequent default or breach of the same or any other term, covenant, or condition. 171	**Section 13.1 --- Condemnation**
172	
173	If all or any portion of the Premises is taken by eminent domain, condemnation, or any similar governmental action (a \"Taking\"):
174	
175	> \(a\) **Major Taking.** If the Taking affects more than twenty-five percent (25%) of the Premises or the Improvement Area, or if the remaining Premises are insufficient, in Tenant\'s reasonable judgment, to permit economically viable operation of the Project, Tenant may terminate this Lease by delivering sixty (60) days\' prior written notice to Landlord, effective as of the date of the Taking.
176	>
177	> \(b\) **Minor Taking.** If the Taking affects twenty-five percent (25%) or less of the Premises and the Improvement Area, and the remaining Premises are sufficient, in Tenant\'s reasonable judgment, to permit continued operation of the Project, this Lease shall continue in full force and effect, and Base Rent shall be equitably adjusted to reflect the reduction in the acreage of the Premises.
178	>
179	> \(c\) **Condemnation Award.** In any Taking, (i) Tenant shall be entitled to receive that portion of the condemnation award or compensation attributable to the value of the Tenant Improvements, the value of Tenant\'s leasehold interest, relocation costs, and lost profits or business interruption, and (ii) Landlord shall be entitled to receive the portion of the award attributable to the value of the underlying land and Landlord\'s reversionary interest. Each Party shall have the right to participate independently in any condemnation proceeding and to make a separate claim for compensation.

182	
183	Neither Party shall be deemed to be in default under this Lease, or shall be liable to the other Party, for any failure or delay in the performance of any obligation hereunder (other than the payment of Rent, except as otherwise provided in Section 4.6) to the extent that such failure or delay is caused by Force Majeure. The Party claiming Force Majeure shall (a) promptly give written notice to the other Party of the occurrence, nature, and expected duration of the Force Majeure event, and (b) use commercially reasonable efforts to mitigate the effects of such event and resume performance as soon as reasonably practicable. If a Force Majeure event prevents Tenant from operating the Project in any material commercial capacity for a continuous period exceeding three hundred sixty-five (365) days, Tenant may terminate this Lease upon ninety (90) days\' prior written notice to Landlord, subject to Tenant\'s Decommissioning obligations under Article 14.

186	
187	If, after the Effective Date, any change in applicable federal, state, or local law, regulation, ordinance, or governmental order (including the adoption of new laws or the repeal or material amendment of existing laws) renders the continued construction or operation of the Project on the Premises commercially impracticable or economically unviable, as reasonably determined by Tenant in good faith (taking into account the totality of the circumstances, including available mitigation measures), Tenant may terminate this Lease upon one hundred eighty (180) days\' prior written notice to Landlord, subject to Tenant\'s Decommissioning obligations under Article 14. 190	
191	Upon any termination by Tenant under this Article 13, Tenant shall (a) pay all Rent and other monetary obligations accrued and unpaid through the effective date of termination, (b) complete Decommissioning and Restoration in accordance with Article 14 within the Decommissioning Period, and (c) have no further liability or obligation under this Lease, except for obligations that by their terms expressly survive termination.

194	
195	**Section 14.1 --- Decommissioning Obligation**
196	
197	Upon the expiration or earlier termination of this Lease (other than a termination resulting from a Taking of the entire Premises, in which case the condemning authority shall be responsible for removal), Tenant shall, at Tenant\'s sole cost and expense, remove all Tenant Improvements from the Premises and restore the surface of the Premises to a condition reasonably comparable to its condition as of the Effective Date, allowing for ordinary wear and tear, natural changes in vegetation, changes in topography resulting from permitted grading operations, and changes resulting from the normal operation of a solar energy facility over the Term (collectively, the \"Decommissioning\" and \"Restoration\"). Tenant shall have a period of eighteen (18) months following the expiration or earlier termination of this Lease (or such longer period as may be necessitated by Force Majeure, governmental permitting requirements, or seasonal limitations on revegetation) to complete all Decommissioning and Restoration activities (the \"Decommissioning Period\").
198	
199	**Section 14.2 --- Scope of Restoration**
200	
201	Restoration shall include, without limitation, the following:
202	
203	> \(a\) Removal of all above-ground structures, including solar panels, racking and tracker systems, inverters, transformers, substations, BESS components, fencing, gates, security equipment, meteorological towers, and all other above-ground improvements;
204	>
205	> \(b\) Removal of all foundations, piles, piers, and footings to a depth of not less than thirty-six (36) inches below finished grade;
206	>
207	> \(c\) Removal of all underground cables, conduit, and wiring to a depth of not less than thirty-six (36) inches below finished grade; cables and conduit buried deeper than thirty-six (36) inches may be abandoned in place unless required to be removed by applicable law or governmental order;
208	>
209	> \(d\) Regrading of all disturbed areas to a condition that is reasonably compatible with surrounding terrain and that provides adequate drainage;
210	>
211	> \(e\) Revegetation of all disturbed areas with a native seed mix appropriate for the Lancaster, California region, in consultation with a qualified restoration ecologist; and
212	>
213	> \(f\) Removal of all construction debris, waste, and hazardous materials from the Premises in compliance with all applicable environmental laws.
214

216	
217	\(a\) No later than the tenth (10th) anniversary of the Commencement Date, Tenant shall deliver to Landlord financial assurance for Tenant\'s Decommissioning obligations in the form of a surety bond or irrevocable standby letter of credit (at Tenant\'s election) in an amount equal to one hundred percent (100%) of the estimated total cost of Decommissioning and Restoration of the Premises (\"Decommissioning Security\"). The surety bond or letter of credit shall be issued by an institution meeting the credit rating requirements set forth in Section 5.1.

    heading(doc,"3.C Landlord Reserved Rights: Minerals, Agriculture, Water and Access (Art. 8; §2.1)",2)
    para(doc,"**Mineral rights (§8.2).** Landlord reserves all mineral, oil, gas, geothermal and subsurface rights and may develop them or lease them to third parties \"without restriction and without the prior consent of Tenant,\" with express rights for Landlord and its lessees to use the surface; Tenant may not interfere. This is the opposite of the Playbook minimum (\"no surface use\" covenant; in Kern County, Tenant approval of subsurface extraction plans that could cause subsidence or vibration), Cascade §6 (\"no surface use\" covenant required; no third-party interference with collateral), and AR §2.4 (No Surface Use Covenant running with the land, Lease controls in any conflict). The risk is not theoretical: per the Cheng Email, Colleen Hargrove-Díaz disclosed that Randall Hargrove has been in discussions with an oil and gas exploration company about leasing mineral rights on portions of the 14,200-acre ranch, including parcels overlapping APNs 287-041-12 and -15. **Severity: CRITICAL.**",align="justify")
    para(doc,"**Agricultural reservation (§8.1).** Landlord may farm, graze, irrigate and apply pesticides/herbicides anywhere outside the Improvement Area, may license third parties to do so, has no duty to coordinate, and Tenant accepts dust, runoff and pesticide drift. (The Cheng Email describes the reservation as applying to land not \"actively occupied\" by solar equipment; the Draft'"'"'s actual test is land outside the Improvement Area on Exhibit B, which has not been prepared — the practical scope therefore depends on how broadly Exhibit B is drawn.) The Playbook (§11.2) requires a complete prohibition for projects ≥50 MW (agrivoltaics not acceptable); Cascade §6 prohibits reserved agricultural/grazing rights inconsistent with project operations; AR §2.4 prohibits all agricultural operations and grazing during the Term. NREL data cited by Development indicate 2%–5% output loss from agricultural dust alone. **Severity: CRITICAL.**",align="justify")
    para(doc,"**Water (§8.3).** Tenant has no right to use any water on or appurtenant to the Premises except on terms and pricing set by Landlord in its sole discretion. Construction-phase dust control (and likely CUP conditions), fire suppression, and periodic module washing all require water; the clause creates a hold-up right. Neither the Playbook nor Cascade addresses water expressly; AR §8.5 grants Tenant the right to install water lines. **Recommend:** Tenant right to use existing wells/water at a pre-agreed rate (or to truck water in and install temporary storage), with priority for construction dust control and fire safety, consistent with the applicable groundwater sustainability plan. **Severity: HIGH.**",align="justify")
    para(doc,"**Landlord access (§8.4).** Landlord and its agents, lessees, licensees and invitees may enter any part of the Premises, including the energized Improvement Area, at any time, without notice, for any purpose \"deemed necessary or desirable by Landlord,\" and Tenant may not condition access. This is a serious safety and OSHA/NEC/NFPA issue (600V DC to 34.5kV AC; lockout/tagout). Playbook §11.1 and AR §2.5: 48 hours'"'"' written notice (email permitted), business hours, compliance with Tenant safety plan, Tenant escort within the Improvement Area, emergency exception with after-the-fact notice. **Severity: HIGH.**",align="justify")
    para(doc,"**Recommended position.** Insert AR §2.4 verbatim (adapted): No Surface Use Covenant binding Landlord and all persons claiming by, through or under Landlord, running with the land, recorded in the Memorandum (AR Ex. E ¶6), with the Lease controlling over any mineral lease; add Kern-County-specific protections — no drilling pads or directional-drilling entry points within a buffer of the Premises boundary, no extraction causing subsidence/vibration, Tenant approval (not unreasonably withheld) of any extraction plan that could affect the Premises, and Landlord indemnity for mineral-lessee interference. Require a Landlord representation that no mineral lease, option or other surface-use right has been granted and covenant that any future mineral lease will be expressly subject to the Lease and the No Surface Use Covenant. Delete §8.1 and replace with a full agricultural/grazing prohibition across all 1,240 acres (vegetation management by Tenant; sheep grazing only at Tenant'"'"'s election under Tenant'"'"'s control, if desired). Conform §8.4 to AR §2.5. **Diligence:** order a title report and mineral-ownership search now; if any mineral estate is severed and held by third parties, the Landlord covenant will not bind them and a surface-use/accommodation agreement (or title insurance endorsement coverage) will be needed.",align="justify")

    # --------------- D FINANCEABILITY
    heading(doc,"3.D Financeability: Lender Protections, Transfers, Forfeiture, Cure and Termination",2)
    para(doc,"**Lender protections (Art. 17).** Estoppel (§17.1), SNDA (§17.2), Leasehold Mortgagee protections (§17.3) and Financing Cooperation (§17.4) are each \"Reserved — Intentionally Omitted.\" The Playbook (§7) states there is no acceptable range: all five protections are required; Cascade §3 requires (i) estoppels within 15 business days with deemed confirmation on failure; (ii) SNDA within 15 business days (non-disturbance against any fee mortgage); (iii) copies of default notices, lender cure periods of 60 days (monetary) and 90 days (non-monetary) **after expiry of Tenant'"'"'s cure period**, extended for foreclosure, no termination without lender notice and cure, and a **new-lease** obligation on termination; and (iv) financing cooperation, with failure constituting a Landlord default. AR Article 10 contains all of these (plus no amendment or voluntary termination without mortgagee consent, AR §10.2(d)), although AR'"'"'s lender cure periods are shorter (30/60 days) than Cascade now requires. **Severity: CRITICAL.**",align="justify")
    para(doc,"**Assignment and encumbrance (§§10.1–10.4).** Consent in Landlord'"'"'s \"sole and absolute discretion\"; \"encumbrance\" expressly includes any leasehold mortgage or deed of trust, so the Draft **prohibits project financing outright**; any unconsented transfer is void and an Event of Default; change of control at any tier of ownership (including fund and tax-equity levels) is an assignment; the original Tenant remains jointly and severally liable for the full Term including extensions; and every assignment costs $25,000 plus Landlord'"'"'s costs. Cascade §2 requires reasonableness, no-consent/no-fee permitted transfers (affiliates, collateral assignment and foreclosure transfers, sale of all/substantially all assets, and **tax-equity transfers** — a category the Playbook does not list but Cascade requires), no upstream change-of-control trigger, release of the original Tenant, and notice within 30 days after a permitted transfer. AR §§9.1–9.4 and 10.1 provide all of this except the tax-equity carve-out (AR includes tax equity investors as Leasehold Mortgagees). **Severity: CRITICAL.**",align="justify")
    para(doc,"**Forfeiture of Improvements (§14.3(d); §§11.2, 12.3(b)).** On termination for an Event of Default, all Improvements \"immediately and automatically\" become Landlord'"'"'s property without compensation, with an irrevocable waiver by Tenant. Separately, Improvements remaining after the six-month Decommissioning Period vest in Landlord (§11.2) and Landlord may elect to retain Improvements on a late decommissioning (§12.3(b)). Cascade §5.2 is absolute: no provision under which Improvements become Landlord'"'"'s property \"upon default, termination, expiration, or any other event,\" however characterized; Cascade also requires a 12-month post-termination lender removal right (§5.4) and UCC fixture-filing consent with a landlord-lien waiver (§5.5). The Playbook (§9.3) treats forfeiture as \"never acceptable\" and likely an unenforceable penalty; a Landlord option to require Improvements be left in place at the end of the Term is acceptable. AR §§11.1–11.3 and 12.4 prohibit any forfeiture and waive any landlord lien. Note that §11.2 combined with the 6-month Decommissioning Period and 15-day cure period creates a practical vesting risk even absent a default termination. **Severity: CRITICAL.**",align="justify")
    para(doc,"**Defaults, cure and remedies (§§14.1–14.3).** A uniform 15-calendar-day cure period for all defaults (Playbook: \"unacceptable under any circumstances\"; Cascade: 30 days monetary / 60 days non-monetary with extension for diligent cure); failure to pay \"when due\" is itself an Event of Default; bankruptcy dismissal window of 60 days (AR: 90); abandonment after only 90 days of inactivity with no Force Majeure, interconnection-wait, repowering or maintenance carve-out (AR §12.1(d): 12 months, with carve-outs); re-entry \"with or without process of law\"; and acceleration of all Rent for the remainder of the Term — including any Extension Term Landlord \"determines would have been exercised\" — discounted at 5%, with credit only for amounts \"actually received\" from reletting. **Severity: CRITICAL (cure periods) / HIGH (remedies).**",align="justify")
    para(doc,"**Termination rights (§§15.1–15.2; Art. 16).** Tenant has no termination right for any reason and waives Civil Code §§1932–1933; on condemnation, Landlord takes the entire award, Rent is not reduced on a partial taking, and Tenant cannot terminate. Playbook §9.2 and Cascade §6 require Tenant termination for (a) condemnation affecting >25% of the Premises or rendering the Project unviable, (b) Force Majeure continuing >365 consecutive days, and (c) change in law rendering the Project unlawful or economically unviable; AR §§13.1–13.3 contain all three plus award allocation and equitable rent reduction. Lacking these rights, the lease is a take-or-pay obligation even if the Project can never be built or operated. We also recommend (beyond the Playbook) a Tenant right to terminate on notice during the Option Period if interconnection, permitting or financing proves infeasible, with Option Period Rent as Landlord'"'"'s sole compensation. **Severity: CRITICAL.**",align="justify")
